summary.intent: Build a hackathon product (Lighthouse / ask-soony) for the Lio 'Keep the Line Running' challenge: analyze Soony's confidential supply data, detect hidden launch risks, and have agents act on them, then polish it for the Sunday 12:00 hand-in.
summary.outcome: Found that Collector's Edition misses launch despite an 'all ok' plan, built a poller, extraction and recheck-and-act product with Felix and Maren role views, History, Fixed today and routines, and merged PR #8. Latest changes are committed on main but not pushed, live server not restarted, and the deck is not built.

repo: Portal API has only /files, /files/{path} and /archive.zip, with no webhooks; changes are detected by polling and comparing SHA-256 checksums, and files can be replaced under the same name.
Confidential portal data must stay in gitignored data/; PR #8 merged 335 files under data/portal into main anyway, though their content matches the portal checksums.
Demo instance (:8001) intentionally runs without a portal token so data cannot change mid-demo; live (:8000) polls the portal. The heartbeat flag now reuses the runner's own token check.
Team workflow requires CLAUDE.md/PROGRESS.md claims and Entire checks (entire status, entire brain status) before pushing.
Roles are Felix (senior buyer, sees all cases and Routines) and Maren (head of procurement, sees For you / All open, History, no Routines); the sign-in names come from portal data.
Outbox sync must append under api._lock, otherwise it overwrote concurrently written approvals.

code.finding: The only merge conflict between llm-task-update and main: both sides added tests at the same spot; keeping both resolved it, and 360 tests pass.
New History page showing who decided what, how and when, grouped by day, with a 'With files read' filter; activity items now record who decided.

workflow: Verify claims against the data first; the subagent cross-check of 200 order confirmations and 59 scans found the 80,000 art book overbooking and the failed statue lot.
Use read-only preview servers and headless screenshots to check UI changes without touching the live instance.
Do not push to a teammate's branch or open PRs with confidential data without explicit user approval.
Users prefer names kept with roles added, not replaced; confirm interpretation of ambiguous UI feedback before building.

friction: Entire initially looked like it hadn't fired because it skips checkpoints when no repo files change.
Heartbeat 'Not checked since 08:30' looked broken on the demo instance, which never polls the portal.
I replaced names with roles when the user wanted roles added, and Maren's own button wrongly read 'Ask Maren to approve'.
The first 'Fixed today' version wrongly listed Boise's 36,000 cards, which arrive after launch.
Realtime phone calls cut out because of noise, concurrent responses and sideband disconnects.
The portal data got into main via PR #8 despite the challenge rules.
The demo background loop does not auto-raise call alerts.
open_items: Push main (about 12 commits ahead of origin) and restart the live server so the sign-in choice, Waiting for your OK and heartbeat appear.
Build the pitch deck and video before the 12:00 hand-in, using Lio figures, the network map and Maren's 'We find out at the dock' quote.
Decide whether to remove data/portal from main (git rm -r --cached data/portal), knowing it stays in history.
Make the 'Fixed today' decisions line open History, committed in the last step but not verified.
Switch the OpenAI webhook back to https://ask-soony.stenglein.dev/hooks/openai after the demo.
Delete the duplicate routine 'Ask Hamburg to count book stock' on live, fix the demo loop's call alerts, and add a Maren top-bar variant.
Delete or keep the earlier Claude doc, and register sender addresses in portal Settings.
